matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the integer values of both sides of the equation, find the numeric difference, and then look for a single‑stick move that changes a numeral or operator by exactly that amount. This ensures the stick move directly addresses the imbalance rather than being arbitrary.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you have exactly one stick to relocate.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral to an operator without first checking how the numeric values change, leaving the equation still false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, increase its value by 5 by repositioning one of its diagonal sticks so that the V becomes an X. The moved stick is reused within the same numeral, preserving the total stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to raise a numeral’s value by 5 and a V is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from a V and discarding it, leaving an invalid V shape, instead of repositioning it to form an X.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: To turn a plus sign into a minus sign, remove its vertical stick and attach that stick as a solitary I to a numeral that can accept an extra I. This keeps the total number of sticks constant and leaves both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a ‘+’ that must become ‘‑’ and there is a numeral able to receive an extra I.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘+’ to ‘‑’ by removing the vertical stick and not using it elsewhere, resulting in a missing stick.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains more than one I (vertical stick), you can move one I from that numeral to another numeral that can accept an extra I, adjusting the values by ±1 while keeping all numerals valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric adjustment is a multiple of 1 and there are numerals with redundant I sticks.
matchstick.example: Taking an I from a numeral that would become empty, making the source numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: To convert a minus sign into an equals sign, you need a second horizontal stick; take it from a numeral that can lose a horizontal stick without becoming invalid and attach it to the minus sign. Ensure the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after the removal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation needs an extra ‘=’ and a ‘‑’ is present, and a suitable numeral can spare a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Adding a horizontal stick from a V (which has no horizontals) to turn ‘‑’ into ‘=’, leaving the V invalid.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: Changing a minus sign to a plus sign requires adding a vertical stick; obtain it from a numeral that can lose an I without becoming invalid, and attach it to the minus sign. The source numeral must stay a valid Roman numeral after the transfer.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace ‘‑’ with ‘+’ and a spare vertical stick is available.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘‑’ to ‘+’ by adding a vertical stick but forgetting to remove it from a numeral, creating an extra stick.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: You can exchange a minus sign and an equals sign by moving one horizontal stick from the ‘=’ to the ‘‑’. The ‘=’ becomes a single‑horizontal minus, and the ‘‑’ becomes a double‑horizontal equals, preserving the total stick count and keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both a ‘‑’ and an ‘=’ and swapping them might resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Swapping ‘‑’ and ‘=’ but then assuming the new equation is correct without recomputing the numeric values.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate any stick from the equality sign, you must still have two horizontal sticks left to form a valid ‘=’, or you must create a new ‘=’ elsewhere. Otherwise the equation loses its required equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you move a stick that belongs to the ‘=’ sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’, leaving only one horizontal and no other ‘=’, resulting in an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears, decrease its value by 5 by repositioning one of its diagonal sticks so that the X becomes a V. This single‑stick move reduces the numeral’s value while keeping the shape valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to lower a numeral’s value by 5 and an X is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X without repositioning it, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as removable, ignoring that some numerals need all their sticks to stay a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only remove sticks from numerals that have redundant sticks (e.g., numerals with multiple I's or V/X when converting between them) and verify that the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after the move.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the rush to relocate a stick, the model forgets to keep the full left‑side, '=', and right‑side structure of the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, explicitly check that the expression still contains a left operand, a single ‘=’, and a right operand, each composed of valid Roman numerals and operators.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes the shape of the operator but neglects the extra vertical component needed for a plus sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting ‘‑’ to ‘+’, source a vertical stick from a numeral that can spare one and attach it to the minus sign, ensuring both the new plus and the source numeral stay valid.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes sticks are interchangeable regardless of orientation, treating diagonal sticks as if they could become vertical or horizontal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: only vertical sticks can form I or the vertical part of a plus, horizontal sticks for minus/equals, and diagonal sticks for V or X.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a horizontal from ‘=’ without ensuring the remaining part still constitutes a proper equality operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from ‘=’, either leave two horizontals behind or create a new ‘=’ elsewhere so the equation retains exactly one valid equality sign.
